name: Zohran Mamdani
summary: Advocate for housing justice and progressive reforms
bio: Zohran Kwame Mamdani is a New York State Assemblymember and democratic socialist running for Mayor. Born in Uganda and raised in New York City, he has fought for the working class in and outside the legislature: hunger striking alongside taxi drivers to achieve more than $450 million in transformative debt relief, winning over $100 million in the state budget for increased subway service and a successful fare-free bus pilot, and organizing New Yorkers to defeat a proposed dirty power plant. Mamdani believes that government can lower costs and make life easier in our city — he will use every tool available to bring down the rent, create world class public transit, and make it easier to raise a family.

name: Alvin Bragg
summary: Focus on criminal justice reform and community safety
bio: Alvin Bragg is focused on ensuring a fair, transparent, and effective justice system while prioritizing community safety. His platform emphasizes reducing gun violence, addressing wrongful convictions, and expanding alternatives to incarceration for nonviolent offenses.

name: Mark Levine
summary: Public health and equitable development champion
bio: Mark Levine advocates for equitable development, climate resilience, and expanded public health infrastructure. He highlights a record of supporting pandemic response efforts, green spaces, and housing initiatives that serve diverse communities.

name: Shaun Abreu
summary: Tenant rights and neighborhood investment priorities
bio: Shaun Abreu focuses on strengthening tenant protections, expanding affordable housing, and investing in public amenities that uplift local neighborhoods. He supports community-driven development and improved city services.

name: Brad Lander
summary: Fiscal accountability and climate resilience initiatives
bio: Brad Lander promotes transparent budgeting, ethical oversight, and investments that prepare the city for climate challenges. He supports auditing programs to improve efficiency and directing funds toward sustainability and equity.

name: Jumaane Williams
summary: Social justice and public safety oversight leader
bio: Jumaane Williams centers his platform on social justice, affordable housing, and accountable public safety oversight. He advocates for community-based violence prevention and expanded access to mental health resources.

name: Cordell Cleare
bio: Cordell Cleare focuses on educational opportunity, public health equity, and environmental justice. Her priorities include school resource investments, healthcare access, and protections against pollution in vulnerable communities.

name: Jordan Wright
summary: Community engagement and youth services focus
bio: Jordan Wright highlights youth services, community engagement, and safer streets. His platform includes expanding after-school programs, supporting small businesses, and improving transportation reliability.

name: Adriano Espaillat
summary: Immigration reform and small business support
bio: Adriano Espaillat emphasizes humane immigration policy, support for small businesses, and equitable economic development. He advocates for pathways to citizenship and investment in local entrepreneurial ecosystems.

name: Yusef Salaam
summary: Justice system reform and youth empowerment
bio: Yusef Salaam is committed to justice system reform, restorative approaches to public safety, and mentorship opportunities for youth. He supports policies that reduce recidivism and expand educational pathways.
